output_examples.input: What FDA pathway do I need for my medical device?
output: FDA pathways include: 510(k) for substantially equivalent devices, PMA for high-risk devices, De Novo for novel devices, and IDE for clinical investigations
Determination depends on: product classification (Class I/II/III), intended use, technological characteristics, and predicate devices
Most Class II devices require 510(k) clearance; Class III devices typically require PMA approval

output_examples.input: What is required for QSR compliance?
output: 21 CFR Part 820 QSR requires: Quality Manual, Design Controls, Document Control, Purchasing Controls, Production Controls, Inspection/Testing, Corrective/Preventive Actions, and Records Management
Key subsystems: Management Controls, Design Controls, Production & Process Controls, Quality Assurance
FDA conducts routine inspections to verify compliance

best_practices: Start FDA strategy early in product development
Maintain complete documentation from design through production
Conduct regular internal audits for QSR compliance
Stay updated on FDA guidance documents
Engage FDA early through pre-submission meetings when appropriate
anti_patterns: Waiting until product development is complete before considering FDA requirements
Copying predicate device submissions without proper justification

faq.question: What is the difference between 510(k) and PMA?
faq.answer: 510(k) is for devices substantially equivalent to existing legally marketed devices (most Class II). PMA is for high-risk Class III devices requiring rigorous safety and effectiveness data.

faq.question: How long does FDA review take?
faq.answer: 510(k) review typically takes 90-180 days. PMA review takes 6-12 months or longer depending on complexity.

faq.question: What is QMSR?
faq.answer: QMSR (Quality Management System Regulation) is FDA's proposed update to 21 CFR Part 820, harmonizing with ISO 13485:2016.

faq.question: Do I need HIPAA compliance?
faq.answer: HIPAA applies if you handle protected health information (PHI). Medical device manufacturers may need BAA agreements with healthcare providers.

faq.question: What is an IDE?
faq.answer: Investigational Device Exemption allows clinical investigation of devices that are not yet approved for commercial distribution.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. This tool provides regulatory guidance. Consult FDA-registered regulatory consultants or legal counsel for formal submissions.
